coverNote: This reference edition holds every idea, bottleneck, package card and term in full, each sorted by the seven metrics I judge the harness by: throughput, efficiency, token count, token cost, time taken, quality of output and hallucinations. The short edition beside it, `HARNESS-IDEAS-AND-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11-14.pdf`, tells the same story in under 25 pages. Every number carries a tag that says how sure we are of it.
howMade: **How this was compiled.** I followed our orchestration design. Sonnet agents first extracted every idea, bottleneck and term from the sources without judging them, each record with a citation in the form `path:line — quote`. I merged duplicates and sorted the records into themes and work packages. Fresh-context Opus agents then checked all 469 [M] condensed idea records, and every number in the narrative, against the sources; they split out 10 [M] more where one record had swallowed a second idea, and I set aside one record about FixFlow’s own product features, which gives the 478 [M] ideas in Part 3. 268 [M] idea records and 11 [M] narrative claims were corrected or tightened, and the corrected text is what is printed here. Last, nine fresh-context readers read the draft as a newcomer would and raised 317 [M] points on clarity, numbers and tone; I applied nearly all of them. Where the record does not know something, this compile says so. Throughout, “I” is me and “we” is the team. **What changed on 14 November.** I changed the lens to the seven metrics and asked for the ideas that lived only in chat. Agents read all 376 [M] messages I typed in 59 [M] saved sessions and matched 113 [M] ideas, observations and requests against the records: 5 [M] were missing and are now recorded, and one measurement that no record held (MSR-50) joins them: six new ideas, 484 [M] in all. Eight classifier agents sorted all 606 [M] earlier records by metric and cause, and a blind second reading agreed on the main metric for 80 of 101 [M]. Idea records otherwise describe where things stood on 13 November, except those of the split idea (PAR-22, TOK-44, TOK-02, TK-FILL, TK-SUMMARIES, PR-HALLU and package WP12), which carry what WP12 finished on 14 November: the rule, its replay and the set-up of the trial I approved.
heatShows: Review and fix rounds draw the most ideas (145 [M], the Review column’s total), then the orchestrator and lanes (106 [M]). Memory has the most open bottlenecks: 22 [M] of its 23 [M] are open, and 46 [M] ideas from all themes address them, so that is where most of the new work is.
